summary: Use <ul> for a list where order does not matter and <ol> for steps or rankings. Every item goes in its own <li>.
notes: <ol> numbers its items automatically. If you add or remove a step, the numbers update.
A nested list goes inside an <li>. Here the Sensors and Motors list belongs to the Robotics item.
Only <li> elements can be direct children of <ul> or <ol>.
pitfall: Typing the numbers yourself ("1. Fill out...") inside an <ol>. The page then shows each number twice.
